results.title: Label-free Biomedical Imaging and Sensing (LBIS) 2026
results.content: Optical detection methods for label-free imaging and sensing are typically based on internal contrast mechanisms of the sample; for example, its ability to delay the light interacting with the sample due to refractive index changes, or its ability to create unique optical spectroscopic, auto-fluorescence, and birefringence or acoustic signatures. We present dynamic spectrally encoded confocal microscopy (D-SECM), a high-speed, label-free imaging technique for real-time visualization of subcellular metabolic activity. Multispectral imaging (MSI) enables label-free analysis of biological tissues by capturing images across multiple wavelengths, enhancing contrast and biochemical specificity over traditional brightfield microscopy. In contrast, label-free optical imaging enables non-invasive access to phenotypic traits of living cells, keeping them viable and sterile for downstream use. We present a label-free, preparation-free approach to blood-cell imaging based on near-focus interference (NFI) quantitative phase imaging, designed for both pre-clinical and clinical use. Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) based on digital holographic microscopy (DHM), can be combined with microscopes and provides label-free access of biophysical cell properties and morphology.

results.content: I lead the Quantum Layered Matter Group at Tel Aviv University, where we investigate electronic and structural phases in two-dimensional (2D) materials, primarily through low-temperature transport and surface probe microscopy. In the talk I will review this topic, show some results (D-wave and laser systems), discuss what we do/don't understand, and try to provide some intuition on what physical mechanisms are expected to give real benefits. I will show both ionization-induced dynamics that are initiated by ultrafast EUV pulses,[1] as well dynamics that are initiated by the mutual neutralization of molecular anions and cations in merged-beams experiments.[2,3] Furthermore, I will discuss our efforts to achieve direct comparison of experimental and theoretical studies towards a better understanding of time-evolving small quantum systems. results.content: The NewU Early College Public Charter School program design, grade level bands, and collaboration with NewU University are born out of this design thinking approach to serve the needs of students and parents in the District and potentially expand it nation-wide. DC students will be educated tuition-free both during their high school/early college years and during the optional one extra year leading to a NewU University Bachelor's. It also guarantees that the School and the University deliver on their respective nonprofit purposes and missions so that the students and parents of DC benefit from the Early College high school program as optimally designed to lead to a Bachelor’s degree in just one tuition-free year after high school.
